To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the multipole representation of the chamber fields does not converge to a good approximation of the exact chamber fields and the initial amplitudes of the particle motion in the horizontal plane are larger than the chamber half aperture for the exact chamber fields.
(1) the multipole representation of the eddy currents is inadequate to describe particle motion in the AGS Booster, and (2) the eddy current compensation coils do not work as designed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an accurate model of the AGS booster vacuum chamber.

the development of a new method of calculating the magnetic field produced in a conducting structure by eddy currents induced in that structure by a beam of charged particles moving in the presence of a magnetic field.

the development and application of a new method for solving the problem of calculating the magnetic field produced in a vacuum chamber by the eddy currents induced in the chamber by a time dependent field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

multipole expansion of the chamber field should be used only for the innermost part of the chamber, and the exact form of chamber field should be employed when the particle motion is to be calculated for the outer part.
multipole expansion of the chamber field should be used for calculations in the region X < 30 mm.
the use of the multipole expansion of the chamber field to calculate the particle motion is not justified and that the particle motion must be calculated using the exact form.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multipole expansion of the eddy field of the AGB Booster does not give the correct field and the exact form of eddy field is necessary.
we have shown that the eddy current model is not adequate for the Booster and that we need to use a model that takes into account the actual geometry of the Booster.
the multipole expansion does not converge for X > 30cm and the exact form does not give the correct initial amplitudes for X < 30cm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the multipole representation of the chamber does not converge to higher multipoles when X > 40 mm.
the multipole expansion is not sufficient to describe the field of the AGs Booster vacuum chamber.
the multipole expansion of the chamber field used in our tracking code does not converge to higher order multipoles and therefore limits the acceptance of the machine.
